english: Last summer we went to the Black Sea coast.
tip: Geçen yaz = last summer. geçen (passing) marks the previous one: geçen hafta (last week), geçen yıl (last year).

english: Hopefully we'll pass the exam, we studied a lot.
tip: geçeriz is the aorist used for a hopeful outcome after İnşallah (hopefully). The aorist also covers likely future events.

english: We've been working in this shop for three generations.
tip: dükkanda = dükkan + da (in the shop). Add -da or -de to a noun for in, at, or on.

english: I love sitting on the balcony and reading books.
tip: oturup links two verbs: oturup then okumayı (sitting and reading). The -ip ending means and then, borrowing the last verb's tense.

english: I can speak Turkish but I struggle with writing.
tip: yazmakta = in writing: -mak (to write) plus -ta (at). zorlanıyorum joins it to mean I struggle at doing it.

english: I drank the tea but didn't drink the coffee.
tip: içmedim is the negative past of içtim: iç + me + dim (I did not drink). The -me before -dim flips it to negative.

english: I don't know this road, let's look at the map.
tip: bakalım = let's look. The -alım or -elim ending on a verb makes a let's suggestion: gidelim, bakalım.

english: We won't work tomorrow.
tip: çalışmayacağız ends in ğ, not k: the k of the future -acak softens to ğ before the vowel ending -ız.

english: You don't read at home.
tip: okumuyorsun hides the negative: before -yor the -ma of oku-ma narrows to -mu, so oku + mu + yor + sun.

english: We aren't coming from the kitchen.
tip: mutfaktan means from the kitchen: the from ending is -tan after a voiceless k, and -dan after voiced sounds.

english: You read a poem usually.
tip: şiir carries no accusative ending here: an unmarked object means poetry in general, not one specific poem.

english: We came home yesterday.
tip: geldik means we came: -di marks a past action you witnessed, and the final -k is the we ending.

english: Could I see the menu, please?
tip: görebilir miyim means may I see: the -ebil inside gör-ebil-ir marks can or be able to do something.

target: Bu yemeğin içinde et var mı?
english: Is there meat in this food?
tip: Turkish needs no verb for is there: et var mı literally asks meat there-is?, using var plus the question word mı.

target: Hem çalışıyorum hem de üniversiteye gidiyorum.
english: I'm both working and going to university.
tip: hem ... hem de means both ... and: it brackets the two actions, hem çalışıyorum hem de gidiyorum.

english: He doesn't go to the beach.
tip: plaja means to the beach: adding -a to plaj marks motion toward something. Front-vowel words take -e instead.

english: They park their cars in the garage.
tip: arabalarını stacks endings: araba + lar (plural) + ı (their) + accusative, meaning their cars as a definite object.

english: You will arrive at the hotel soon.
tip: varacaksınız = var + acak + sınız, you will arrive: future uses -acak after back vowels, -ecek after front ones.

english: The firefighters are trying to put out the fire.
tip: söndürmeye çalışıyor means trying to put out: the verb takes -meye (to) before çalışmak, to try.

english: The cat's fur sticks everywhere.
tip: Kedinin tüyleri means the cat's fur: kedi takes the genitive -nin (of the cat) and tüy takes the possessive -leri (its).

english: Take care, the weather is cold.
tip: dikkat et is the informal command take care: the bare verb stem alone tells one person to do something.

english: Eighty percent of students passed the exam.
tip: geçmiş uses -mış, the reported past: it frames students passed as hearsay or inference, not something you personally saw.

target: Pahalı bir restoran yerine ucuz ve lezzetli bir lokanta bulduk.
english: Instead of an expensive restaurant we found a cheap and delicious eatery.
tip: yerine follows the noun to mean instead of it: restoran yerine = instead of a restaurant.

english: Do you know what time the shop closes?
tip: kapandığını turns a whole clause into an object: -dığı plus accusative lets you say know what time it closed.

english: I've been living in this city for a quarter of a century.
tip: asırdır adds -dır meaning for: çeyrek asırdır = for a quarter century, marking how long the action has gone on.

target: Geçen yaz ailece Antalya'ya tatile gittik.
english: Last summer we went on vacation to Antalya as a family.
tip: ailece means as a family: adding -ce to aile makes an adverb, the whole group doing it together.

target: Balıkçı her sabah göl kenarında sabırla balık tutuyor.
english: The fisherman patiently fishes by the lake every morning.
tip: sabırla means patiently: the -la ending (with) turns the noun sabır (patience) into a manner adverb.

target: Günaydın komşu, bugün hava çok güzel değil mi?
english: Good morning neighbor, the weather is really nice today, isn't it?
tip: değil mi is the tag isn't it: değil means not, so güzel değil mi asks nice, no?, inviting agreement.

target: Kedimiz her gün bahçede dolaşır ve kuşları izler.
english: Our cat walks around the garden every day and watches the birds.
tip: dolaşır and izler use the aorist (-r or -ir): this tense states habits and routines, not an action happening right now.

target: Okul ile ev arasında bir park var, oradan geçiyorum.
english: There's a park between the school and home, I pass through there.
tip: arasında means between and follows its nouns: okul ile ev arasında = between school and home, position words come last.
